retained_foundations: GRT73–77 identify the ordinary PEL model, the abelian period and section frames of the selected generic object, and a common dense open on the model normalized in its actual component field. The two cutoffs use one underlying model. To apply GRT74 and GRT67 integrally, the smooth semiabelian group, polarization and ample section frames on its boundary must agree with the original family and with the model used by the height comparisons at each required member and level.

GRT71 proves that all finite-extension classical tests detect the actual completed ideal. GRT72 proves independence of the period labels after the realized tests are identified with one marked uniformizing chart. The comparison of these tests, with their rigidified group, torus, and polarization, must hold for the selected degeneration at each centre.

The applicable arithmetic intersection and resolution system, its projection formula and changes of metric remain inputs. GRT34 computes the two Newton identities, GRT52 the uniform determinant, and GRT57 the fixed-tower wall height on this system.

formal_consumer.scope: GRT37–57 give the determinant and wall height estimates on the marked model. GRT58–66 prove descent of its boundary ideal, the precise leading-term and sharp theta bounds, and persistence of the dividing coordinate on compatible marked charts. GRT67–69 glue local models, recover the generic family up to finite extension, and compare the period lattices of classical lifts. GRT70 proves tameness of the auxiliary marking stabilizer on the designated prime-to-level charts. GRT71–72 detect divisibility in the completed stalk and identify period labels across its realized tests. GRT73–74 give the separate finite maps from the abelian open to the ordinary marked space and from that space to Siegel moduli. GRT75–77 identify the selected abelian periods, section bases and a common dense open in the actual component field. The remaining comparisons at the boundary and on the arithmetic intersection system are recorded below.
